article_title: Alibaba Open-Sources OpenCodeReview, an AI Code-Review CLI It Says Beats Claude Code on Precision, as Reviewers Flag a 20% Recall Ceiling
summary: Chief Editor override: automated REJECT was triggered by a false-positive prompt-injection match (an unrelated related-articles JSON widget on the InfoQ page, not an instruction to an AI agent). Manual source review found the article's central Alibaba-vs-Claude-Code claims and the Vaughan recall-ceiling quote to be accurately and verbatim attributed, but the Tom Rochette quote about a 12% independent-benchmark precision figure was trimmed in a way that drops material context (the maintainer's dispute and fix). Publishing with a corrections note.

findings.message: Chief Editor manually verified the flagged suspicious_patterns excerpt in the raw snapshot and determined it is a false positive, not a genuine prompt-injection attempt.
findings.details: The exact matched text sits inside a JSON data blob powering an InfoQ 'related articles' recommendation widget: literally '..."url":"/news/2026/09/spotify-gisting-llm-performance","title":"Shopify Introduces Gisting: Compressing LLM System Prompts into Learned Tokens","authorsList":["Sergio De Simone"],"itemPath":"/news/2026/09/spotify-gisting-llm-performance","score":169,...'. This is metadata for an unrelated, separate InfoQ article about LLM prompt-compression technique ('gisting'), listed as a related-content recommendation. findings.message: Rochette quote in the body trims material context that changes how the '12 percent precision' figure should be read.
findings.details: Article renders as a direct quote: "The one independent benchmark run was about 12 percent precision on 10 Martian-benchmark PRs" — a far lower figure than Alibaba's own internal results. The InfoQ snapshot's actual sentence (unabridged) is: "The one independent benchmark run so far was ugly: about 12 percent precision on 10 Martian-benchmark PRs, disputed by the maintainer as a tool-call anomaly and fixed, with no independent post-fix validation." The article's quotation marks present a verbatim-looking excerpt but silently drop the trailing clause noting the maintainer disputed the anomaly and fixed it (with no independent re-validation since). This omission is presented without ellipsis and changes the reader's takeaway: the 12% figure reads as a live, unrebutted contradiction of Alibaba's benchmark rather than a disputed, since-patched anomaly. This is a subordinate body claim, not the headline/summary/lead (the headline's '20% Recall Ceiling' phrase is Vaughan's separate, verbatim-quoted point, which checks out). Filed as a correction rather than REJECT.

content_preview.title: Alibaba Open-Sources OpenCodeReview, an AI Code-Review CLI It Says Beats Claude Code on Precision, as Reviewers Flag a 20% Recall Ceiling
content_preview.summary: Alibaba open-sourced OpenCodeReview, an AI code-review CLI it says outperforms Claude Code on precision using far fewer tokens, while independent reviewers warn of a low recall ceiling and weaker results outside Alibaba's own benchmark.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Alibaba has open-sourced OpenCodeReview, an AI-powered code review CLI that combines deterministic pipelines for file selection, bundling, and rule matching with an LLM agent for dynamic code analysis, according to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/alibaba-opencodereview/). The tool, released under an Apache-2.0 license, ships built-in checks for issues such as null-pointer exceptions, thread safety, XSS, and SQL injection, per [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/ali...

recommendations: Merge with a public corrections record addressing the trimmed Rochette quote (missing 'disputed by the maintainer as a tool-call anomaly and fixed, with no independent post-fix validation' context).

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis sections. Appropriately hedges the precision/F1 claims as chart-derived rather than exact published percentages, and explicitly flags the unresolved question of how Rochette's 'Martian-benchmark' test compares in scope to Alibaba's own 200-PR evaluation. Tone throughout is measured and attributive ('Alibaba states', 'according to InfoQ') rather than asserting the comparison as fact.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from sources/2026-09/alibaba-open-sources-opencodereview-an-ai-code-review-cli-it-says-beats-claude-code-on-precision-as-reviewers-flag-a-20-recall-ceiling/ (not re-fetched). source-0.html.gz (InfoQ, https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/alibaba-opencodereview/, sha256 5a882783c57f7bcfec10e4876ff2e7578981e3106f24559385446ec169e7abeb): confirmed the architecture description, the Apache-2.0 license and built-in rule categories, the 'tens of thousands of Alibaba developers'/two-year internal use claim, the Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/GitHub/GitLab/Gerrit/VS Code/MCP integration list, the Alibaba precision/F1/one-ninth-tokens claim (verbatim match), Tom Rochette's 'senior developer at Shopify' title and his architecture-praise quote (near-verbatim, trivial comma difference only), Daniel Vaughan's 'head of forward deployed engineering at HCLTech' title and both of his quotes (20% recall ceiling quote and 'better harness' conclusion, both verbatim). Found one quote-fidelity issue: Rochette's '12 percent precision on 10 Martian-benchmark PRs' quote in the article omits the source's trailing clause about the maintainer disputing and fixing the anomaly (see Content Accuracy finding above) — filed as a correction. source-1.html.gz (GitHub, https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review, sha256 041b05811d6d0db47dc8b03b8b96088636d4a56320373524a558dda254ee27af): confirmed the repo description string quoted in the article verbatim ('Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.'), the 'served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects' quote verbatim, the benchmark description quote verbatim ('A real-world code review benchmark built from 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real Pull Requests, and 10 programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers (1,505 annotated ground-truth issues).'), and the Apache-2.0 license.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (license, integration list, internal-use duration, benchmark scale figures, both reviewer titles and affiliations, the 20% recall figure, the one-ninth token figure) trace to the cited sources. The one exception is the trimmed Rochette quote described above, which is accurate in substance (12% precision figure is real and attributed correctly to Rochette) but omits context material enough to affect how a reader weighs it. No fabricated specifics found. No orphan source URLs — both cited URLs appear in article.sources and are used in the body; no bidirectional gap.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. The headline's 'It Says' framing correctly marks the precision claim as Alibaba's own assertion rather than the outlet's or this publication's verified fact, and 'Reviewers Flag' correctly marks the recall-ceiling point as external pushback. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of OpenCodeReview or Alibaba's AI code-review tooling found. Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ and src/content/articles/2026-08/ for 'code review'/'code-review' and 'alibaba' matches: found unrelated code-review coverage (Harness, LinkedIn, GitHub Copilot, a Java code-smell study, an MCR-Bench study) and unrelated Alibaba coverage (Qwen-Image 2.1, Thomson Reuters' Qwen-based model) — none overlap with this story's subject, sources, or angle. Genuinely new topic.
concerns: Rochette's '12 percent precision on 10 Martian-benchmark PRs' is rendered in quotation marks as if verbatim but silently drops the source's trailing clause noting the maintainer disputed the finding as a tool-call anomaly and fixed it, with no independent post-fix re-validation. This omission tilts the quote toward reading as an unrebutted contradiction of Alibaba's internal benchmark, when the source frames it as a disputed and since-patched anomaly. Filed as a correction below; does not affect the headline, summary, or lead.
recommendations: File a public corrections record noting the full context of Rochette's 12% precision quote, specifically that the maintainer disputed it as a tool-call anomaly and fixed it, with no independent post-fix validation since.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced News piece on a genuinely new topic with correctly and mostly-verbatim attributed claims on both sides of a contested benchmark comparison. One quote in the body (not the headline/lead) was trimmed in a way that omits material context; a single corrections note can honestly inform readers of the missing context without gutting the article. The automated REJECT was driven by a confirmed false-positive prompt-injection match on an unrelated related-articles data blob, not a genuine integrity problem, and is overridden per the manual verification documented in the findings and Step 3d process. Recommend APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
